'''Drahoslav Lím''' (September 30, 1925, in Czechoslovakia – August 22, 2003, in San Diego, California)<ref>US Social Security Death Index, reported at http://ssdi.rootsweb.ancestry.com/cgi-bin/ssdi.cgi</ref> was a [[Czechs|Czech]] [[chemist]]. He invented [[polyhydroxyethylmethacrylate]], the [[Organic compound#Synthetic_compounds|synthetic material]] used for soft [[contact lenses]] ([[hydrogel]]).

Lím worked<ref>Chain transfer of polymer in radical polymerization. Lim, D.; Wichterle, O. Journal of Polymer Science  (1958),  29  579-84</ref><ref>Intra-cameral lenses made of hydrocolloidal acrylates. Dreifus M.; Wichterle, O.; Lim D.    Ceskoslovenska oftalmologie (1960), 16 154-9.</ref><ref>Tolerance of orbital implants made of hydrocolloid acrylate.     Dreifus M.; Herben T.; Lim D.; Wichterle, O. Sbornik lekar sky (1960), 62 212-8.</ref><ref>On the problem of contact lenses. Wichterle, O.; Lim D.; Dreifus M.  Ceskoslovenska oftalmologie (1961), 17 70-5.</ref> as a member of the team of [[Otto Wichterle]] (the inventor of soft contact lenses) and in 1955, he came up with poly(hydroethyl-acrylate), the material later used for the lenses. This work was later published in Nature<ref name=Wichterle_1960/> and was the subject of US patents.<ref>Otto Wichterle and Drahoslav Lim, "Process for producing shaped articles from three-dimensional hydrophilic high polymers", US Patent 2,976,576, March 28, 1961</ref><ref>Otto Wichterle and Drahoslav Lim, "Cross-linked hydrophilic polymers and articles made therefrom", US Patent 3,220,960, November 30, 1965</ref>  During 1970 to 1974 he worked in [[Palo Alto, California]], improving contact lenses materials and technology.  

When he returned to [[Czechoslovakia]] he was persecuted for political reasons and was not allowed to work in his specialisation. In 1979, he was allowed to emigrate to the United States. There Lím worked on materials for [[artificial kidney]]s and continued with research on [[polymer]]s. He was both a professor at the University of California, San Diego and the de facto founder of the Revlon Materials Research Center. At the latter he led a team of scientists who researched tinting technologies for hydrogel contact lenses, materials for intraocular lenses, and formulations for nail enamel. He was awarded over 150 patents.
